Projet DevDesk (Go, Bubble Tea), répertoire /home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk (branche main, ne modifie aucun code). Conçois le plan d'implémentation de la story DEVDESK-149 « Templates : pastille sur le catalogue » (vue `:templates`, internal/ui/templates, internal/template).

Critères d'acceptation :
1. Le catalogue affiche en première colonne la pastille (colonne d'activité), avec l'icône de la source ou du modèle au repos (la colonne d'icône existe déjà).
2. Synchronisation en cours (ou chargement de fichier) : les lignes concernées clignotent ; à la fin sans erreur, l'icône revient.
3. Échec de scan ou de synchronisation sur une source : ligne ⊗ rouge fixe, le footer donne la cause, un nouvel essai l'efface (kinds relançables depuis templates, D5).
4. Le message de progression de la synchronisation (`jobs.Reporter` avec son case dans le routeur) : `TestEveryJobReporterIsRoutedToTheRegistry` passe toujours.
5. Terminal 60 colonnes : Rule 116 tient ; l'aide `?` porte la légende.
Hors périmètre : les sources et la récupération de fichiers. Aucun spinner de ligne à retirer. Retirer l'entrée de templates de la liste d'exceptions du garde de A-16 (DEVDESK-143, guard de la colonne d'activité).

Modèles déjà livrés à imiter (git log) : DEVDESK-144 (ws, a59eef3), 142 (:jobs + garde, b2c3224), 138 (mémorisateur d'échec par cible dans le registre jobs, 925f045), 147/148 (explorer), 146 (images OCI). Docs : docs/product/activity-indicator/ (stories.md, ux.md, brief.md), docs/architecture/templates.md, app-shell.md, ui-components.md, .claude/rules/tui-*.md. Suis .entire/graph-agent.md (entire graph search d'abord).

Livrable : plan en étapes livrables et testables (fichiers, interfaces, tests à écrire, commandes de tests ciblés), écrit dans .claude/plans/DEVDESK-149-plan.md, plus compte rendu court : résultat, fichiers, risques, Questions bloquantes éventuelles (ne tranche pas à la place de l'utilisateur). Ne relis pas ce que tu n'as pas besoin de lire.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one spinner chain and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci`, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface` |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage` and `internal/ui/datatable` |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

## Dependencies

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# Planning Rules

## Implementation Plans

- **Location**: Always write implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` in the current project directory.
- **Format**: Use Markdown format for plans.
- **Naming**: Use descriptive names like `feature-name-plan.md` or `YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name.md`.

## Antigravity IDE Integration

When using the Antigravity IDE extension:
- Save all implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` relative to the project root.
- Create the directory if it doesn't exist before saving plans.
- Plans should be accessible from both Claude Code CLI and Antigravity IDE.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

Tu es architecte logiciel. Tu conçois ; tu n'implémentes pas (tu n'écris que dans `docs/`).

## Méthode

1. Lis le code existant et les contraintes (`CLAUDE.md`, ADR, infra) avant de proposer.
   Si le brief contient une synthèse du wiki (« Références wiki », produite par
   `dev-team:wiki-scout`), appuie les options dessus et cite-la. Ne parcours pas le wiki
   toi-même : lis au plus une page, à partir d'un chemin donné dans la synthèse, pour
   approfondir un point précis. Sans synthèse, continue normalement.
2. Exprime les exigences non fonctionnelles (charge, sécurité, coût, exploitabilité).
3. Compare au moins deux options avec leurs compromis, puis recommande-en une.
4. Décris composants, interfaces, flux de données, modèle de données, migration.
5. Identifie risques et points irréversibles.

## Documentation à jour (Context7)

Si les outils `mcp__plugin_dev-team_context7__*` sont disponibles, vérifie avec eux les capacités et limites actuelles d'une bibliothèque ou d'un service avant de les recommander :
`resolve-library-id` puis `query-docs`, avec une question précise (une bibliothèque, un
sujet, la version du projet), jamais « toute la documentation ». Sinon, lis le code et les
manifestes du projet, ou demande : ne devine pas une signature d'API.

## Mode faisabilité rapide

Sur un brief produit ou des stories, sans conception détaillée : faisable ou non et à
quelles conditions, risques techniques majeurs, dépendances externes, effort par story
(S / M / L, avec l'hypothèse qui le justifie), stories à redécouper et comment.
Une page au plus ; pas d'ADR ; pas de wiki.

## Sortie (conception)

- Brouillon d'ADR si la décision le mérite (skill `team-core:adr` si disponible : critères,
  gabarit), à archiver par `archivist`.
- Plan d'implémentation : étapes numérotées, chacune livrable et testable seule, avec
  fichiers concernés, interfaces à créer (signatures), comportements à tester
  (entrée → résultat attendu, cas d'erreur), dépendances entre étapes et critère de fin.
  Le `tester` écrit les tests de l'étape avant le code à partir de ces éléments. Signale les étapes
  parallélisables. Un `coder` doit pouvoir réaliser une étape sans relire tout le plan.

## Ne rien supposer

Si une information qui change le résultat manque ou est ambiguë (volumétrie, exigence non fonctionnelle, contrainte d'hébergement, choix qui engage l'utilisateur ; ne chiffre jamais une charge inventée), ne la devine
pas : arrête-toi et rends tes questions en tête de ta sortie, sous **Questions
bloquantes**, chacune avec les options possibles et ta recommandation. L'orchestrateur
les posera à l'utilisateur. Pour un détail sans conséquence, choisis l'option la plus

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- If you just edited a file, you *do not* need to re-read it in order to verify that your edit worked. This is because the Edit/Write tools will throw an error if your change failed, and the harness you are running in already tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Your working directory persists between calls. In general you should prefer absolute paths, because using `cd` in a compound command could trigger a permission prompt for the user. Shell state, such as env vars and functions, does not persist - the shell has been initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

tools.name: Edit

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up to help you perform a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow, certain types of design taste or API interactions, and so on). 1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for

- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent

- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)

- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in

    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

- dev-team:targeted-tests: Lancer seulement les tests liés aux fichiers modifiés, avec une sortie courte. À charger avant de lancer des tests pendant une feature ou un correctif (tester, coder, debugger).

- plane-integration:plane-conventions: Conventions pour suivre epics, stories, tâches et bugs dans Plane avec les agents (identités par rôle, modèle de données, états, limites de l'édition Community). À charger avant toute lecture ou écriture dans Plane via les outils mcp__plane-<rôle>__*.

- engineering:incident-response: Run an incident response workflow — triage, communicate, and write postmortem. Trigger with "we have an incident", "production is down", an alert that needs severity assessment, a status update mid-incident, or when writing a blameless postmortem after resolution.

systemPrompt:
Tu es architecte logiciel. Tu conçois ; tu n'implémentes pas (tu n'écris que dans `docs/`).

## Méthode

1. Lis le code existant et les contraintes (`CLAUDE.md`, ADR, infra) avant de proposer.
   Si le brief contient une synthèse du wiki (« Références wiki », produite par
   `dev-team:wiki-scout`), appuie les options dessus et cite-la. Ne parcours pas le wiki
   toi-même : lis au plus une page, à partir d'un chemin donné dans la synthèse, pour
   approfondir un point précis. Sans synthèse, continue normalement.
2. Exprime les exigences non fonctionnelles (charge, sécurité, coût, exploitabilité).
3. Compare au moins deux options avec leurs compromis, puis recommande-en une.
4. Décris composants, interfaces, flux de données, modèle de données, migration.
5. Identifie risques et points irréversibles.

## Documentation à jour (Context7)

Si les outils `mcp__plugin_dev-team_context7__*` sont disponibles, vérifie avec eux les capacités et limites actuelles d'une bibliothèque ou d'un service avant de les recommander :
`resolve-library-id` puis `query-docs`, avec une question précise (une bibliothèque, un
sujet, la version du projet), jamais « toute la documentation ». Sinon, lis le code et les
manifestes du projet, ou demande : ne devine pas une signature d'API.

## Mode faisabilité rapide

Sur un brief produit ou des stories, sans conception détaillée : faisable ou non et à
quelles conditions, risques techniques majeurs, dépendances externes, effort par story
(S / M / L, avec l'hypothèse qui le justifie), stories à redécouper et comment.
Une page au plus ; pas d'ADR ; pas de wiki.

## Sortie (conception)

- Brouillon d'ADR si la décision le mérite (skill `team-core:adr` si disponible : critères,
  gabarit), à archiver par `archivist`.
- Plan d'implémentation : étapes numérotées, chacune livrable et testable seule, avec
  fichiers concernés, interfaces à créer (signatures), comportements à tester
  (entrée → résultat attendu, cas d'erreur), dépendances entre étapes et critère de fin.
  Le `tester` écrit les tests de l'étape avant le code à partir de ces éléments. Signale les étapes
  parallélisables. Un `coder` doit pouvoir réaliser une étape sans relire tout le plan.

## Ne rien supposer

Si une information qui change le résultat manque ou est ambiguë (volumétrie, exigence non fonctionnelle, contrainte d'hébergement, choix qui engage l'utilisateur ; ne chiffre jamais une charge inventée), ne la devine
pas : arrête-toi et rends tes questions en tête de ta sortie, sous **Questions
bloquantes**, chacune avec les options possibles et ta recommandation. L'orchestrateur
les posera à l'utilisateur. Pour un détail sans conséquence, choisis l'option la plus
prudente et signale-la dans ta sortie (`Hypothèse : …`).

Étant donné une vue qui veut faire clignoter une ligne hors registre (action instantanée `busy`, agent `running`, chargement des enfants d'un groupe), quand le routeur termine un `Update`, alors il l'interroge par une interface optionnelle `WantsBlink() bool` (sur le modèle de `FormView` et `LeavingView`) puis appelle `ensureTick` : signal par niveau, pas par front. Testé avec `go test -race`.
181	7. Étant donné la cadence, quand un spinner de footer en dépend (registre actif), alors le tick bat à 100 ms ; sinon à 500 ms. La phase qui change n'envoie qu'un `jobs.FrameMsg` (sans copie du registre) à la vue à l'écran, plus la phase courante à l'entrée (`switchView`) ; `ChangedMsg` reste réservé aux changements du registre.
182	8. Étant donné la mesure `TEA_TRACE` du coût de redessin à 1 Hz (hypothèse H2), quand la story est livrée, alors le résultat (octets émis par seconde avec 1 et 20 lignes clignotantes) est consigné et transmis à l'utilisateur dans la PR.
183	9. `app-shell.md` décrit le tick (et ce qu'il devient de la chaîne D5) dans le même commit.
184	
185	**Hors périmètre** : les spinners de chargement global du footer (Rule 128) ; ralentir le spinner du footer des jobs ; tout autre mouvement.
186	**Hypothèses** : Hypothèse: envelopper `App.Update` (un `update` interne plus un appel final) est faisable sans casser le spinner du footer ; c'est le risque élevé de la story.
187	**Questions ouvertes** : aucune (fréquence 1 Hz tranchée, D7).
188	
189	### A-04 — Mémorisateur central du dernier échec par cible (DEVDESK-138)
190	Epic : E1 — Priorité : Must — Effort : M
191	
192	En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux que l'échec d'une opération sur une cible reste visible dans les vues qui peuvent la relancer, jusqu'à ce que je réessaie, afin de ne pas perdre un échec en changeant de vue.
193	
194	**Critères d'acceptation**
195	1. Étant donné une opération qui échoue sur une cible dans un contexte, quand l'échec est enregistré, alors le mémorisateur le garde sous la clé (type d'opération, cible, contexte) avec la cause lisible ; au plus un échec par clé. Il vit **dans `jobs.Registry`** : posé par `Apply` (`failed`), effacé par `Start` (la clé est admise) et par `Apply` `done` ; écrit seulement depuis l'`Update` du routeur (Rule 110). Les runs terminés sont élagués au-delà de `MaxFinishedRuns`, le mémorisateur n'en dépend donc pas.
196	2. Étant donné un échec mémorisé, quand la même clé démarre une nouvelle tentative ou réussit, alors l'échec est effacé à cette transition.
197	3. Étant donné un échec mémorisé, quand la cible est supprimée (`jobs.ForgetTargetMsg{Target}` envoyé par une vue pour une suppression hors registre, ou `delete` `done` du registre), alors l'échec est effacé ; quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `ctrl+r` ou quitte puis rouvre la vue, alors l'échec reste.
198	4. Étant donné un échec dans le contexte A, quand l'utilisateur est dans le contexte B, alors cet échec n'est pas montré ; en revenant dans A, il l'est encore.
199	5. Étant donné l'arrêt de l'application, quand elle redémarre, alors aucun échec n'est restauré (aucune écriture disque : test qui vérifie qu'aucun fichier n'est créé). Plafond de 500 clés, les plus anciennes sortent d'abord.
200	6. Étant donné une vue qui lit le mémorisateur, quand elle le fait, alors elle reçoit une copie (`ChangedMsg.Failures`), jamais un pointeur sur l'état du routeur.
201	7. Étant donné les deux copies manuelles actuelles (`security.scanTarget.Failed`, `failedScans` d'OCI), quand cette story est livrée, alors elles sont encore en place ; leur retrait relève de A-08 et A-09a, ce qui garde cette story livrable seule.
202	8. Étant donné la clé, quand deux vues désignent la même cible, alors elles produisent la même clé : `Item.Target` (clé de cache de scan), chemins passés par `filepath.Clean` au lancement ; un dépôt a son chemin absolu en `ws` et dans `:sec`, une image sa référence brute (`repo:tag`) dans OCI et dans `:sec`. Un test de clé commune couvre les images sans tag (`<none>`) et les références écrites autrement (`nginx` contre `docker.io/library/nginx`). Une image et un dépôt ne sont pas la même cible.
203	9. Étant donné D5, quand une vue lit le mémorisateur, alors elle ne retient que les types d'opération qu'elle peut relancer. Table indicative de l'architect : `ws` scan, sync, delete ; `:sec` scan ; OCI scan, pull ; explorer create, delete, clone ; templates scan, sync. Conséquence : un échec de sync dans `ws` n'apparaît pas dans `:sec`. Les types réellement mémorisés restent la question ouverte 2.
204	10. `app-shell.md` décrit le mémorisateur (clé, durée de vie, remplacement des copies manuelles) dans le même commit.
205	
206	**Hors périmètre** : persistance, expiration automatique, échec d'actions instantanées (restent au footer), affichage (A-06 et suivantes).
207	**Questions ouvertes** : identité canonique et types d'opération mémorisés (question ouverte 2).
208	
209	### A-05 — Footer par ligne : ce qui s'exécute, ou la cause de l'erreur (DEVDESK-140)
210	Epic : E1 — Priorité : Must — Effort : M
211	
212	En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux que le footer dise, pour la ligne sélectionnée, ce qui s'exécute ou pourquoi elle est en erreur, afin de comprendre la pastille sans ouvrir `:jobs`.
213	
214	**Critères d'acceptation**
215	1. Étant donné une ligne sélectionnée dont la pastille est « en cours », quand le footer s'affiche, alors il nomme l'opération au niveau `Status` de `components.FooterMessage` (Rule 128), avec le glyphe de la pastille en préfixe en texte brut, selon les phrases validées de `ux.md` §1.2 (ex. `● Scanning ~/w/app/api`).
216	2. Étant donné une ligne sélectionnée en erreur, quand l'échec arrive, alors un `Error` de 3 s le dit (`Failed to scan … — <cause>`) ; ensuite, tant que la ligne est sélectionnée, un `Status` persistant donne la cause lisible (`⊗ <cible>: last scan failed — <cause>`), jamais `err.Error()` brut non rédigé pour l'écran.
217	3. Étant donné une progression globale en cours (« 3/12 ») ou un bilan de sync, quand l'utilisateur sélectionne une ligne, alors la progression et le bilan restent affichés : un seul constructeur dans `components`, à côté de `JobsStatusLine`, compose « détail de ligne · progression globale » et tronque d'abord le détail de ligne (précédence error > warn > info > status inchangée).
218	4. Étant donné un message `Error`, `Warn` ou `Info` avec minuteur, quand il est affiché, alors il prend le pas sur le détail de ligne et celui-ci revient à l'expiration.
219	5. Étant donné une ligne au repos, quand elle est sélectionnée, alors le footer ne montre aucun texte d'activité. Un conteneur `running` garde « Running since 3 hr ago », **sans glyphe en préfixe** (D8).
220	6. Étant donné plusieurs opérations sur la ligne, quand le footer s'affiche, alors il nomme l'état gagnant (priorité de A-01) et, si un échec est masqué, l'ajoute en suffixe (`· earlier failure: sync (see :jobs)`).
221	7. Étant donné un terminal étroit, quand le texte dépasse la largeur, alors il est tronqué proprement et la hauteur du footer ne change pas (Rule 124).
222	8. Le texte est identique pour la même opération dans toutes les vues (un seul constructeur de phrase, test).
223	
224	**Hors périmètre** : le câblage dans chaque vue (fait dans sa story de migration) ; les messages d'actions instantanées.
225	**Questions ouvertes** : aucune (libellés validés, D10).
226	
227	---
228	
229	## Epic E2 — Migration des vues
230	
231	### A-06 — Pilote : `:jobs` avec la pastille, et décision go/no-go sur le clignotement (DEVDESK-142)
232	Epic : E2 — Priorité : Must — Effort : S (+ une semaine d'usage avant la décision)
233	
234	En tant qu'utilisateur de `:jobs`, je veux voir l'état de chaque run et de chaque cible dans la première colonne via la pastille, afin de repérer ce qui tourne et ce qui a échoué, et de juger si le clignotement m'aide avant qu'il soit étendu partout.
235	
236	**Critères d'acceptation**
237	1. Étant donné la table des runs et celle des cibles, quand elles s'affichent, alors la première colonne est la pastille (sans titre, `datatable.IconColumnWidth`, `SizingFixed`, ni `Less` ni `Search`) et le spinner de ligne actuel est supprimé. `:jobs` a déjà la colonne : on remplace le glyphe et on retire la frame.
238	2. Étant donné les issues, quand elles s'affichent, alors `done` est `◉`, `failed` `⊗` (rouge), `cancelled` `⊘`, `skipped` `⊖`, `queued` `◴`, `running` `●`/`○` ; tous différents entre eux ; `done` n'est pas vert.
239	3. Étant donné un run « en cours », quand le tick bat, alors la pastille clignote ; avec `app.motion: static`, elle est `●` fixe (A-02).

### A-04 — Mémorisateur central du dernier échec par cible (DEVDESK-138)
Epic : E1 — Priorité : Must — Effort : M

En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux que l'échec d'une opération sur une cible reste visible dans les vues qui peuvent la relancer, jusqu'à ce que je réessaie, afin de ne pas perdre un échec en changeant de vue.

**Critères d'acceptation**
1. Étant donné une opération qui échoue sur une cible dans un contexte, quand l'échec est enregistré, alors le mémorisateur le garde sous la clé (type d'opération, cible, contexte) avec la cause lisible ; au plus un échec par clé. Il vit **dans `jobs.Registry`** : posé par `Apply` (`failed`), effacé par `Start` (la clé est admise) et par `Apply` `done` ; écrit seulement depuis l'`Update` du routeur (Rule 110). Les runs terminés sont élagués au-delà de `MaxFinishedRuns`, le mémorisateur n'en dépend donc pas.
2. Étant donné un échec mémorisé, quand la même clé démarre une nouvelle tentative ou réussit, alors l'échec est effacé à cette transition.
3. Étant donné un échec mémorisé, quand la cible est supprimée (`jobs.ForgetTargetMsg{Target}` envoyé par une vue pour une suppression hors registre, ou `delete` `done` du registre), alors l'échec est effacé ; quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `ctrl+r` ou quitte puis rouvre la vue, alors l'échec reste.
4. Étant donné un échec dans le contexte A, quand l'utilisateur est dans le contexte B, alors cet échec n'est pas montré ; en revenant dans A, il l'est encore.
5. Étant donné l'arrêt de l'application, quand elle redémarre, alors aucun échec n'est restauré (aucune écriture disque : test qui vérifie qu'aucun fichier n'est créé). Plafond de 500 clés, les plus anciennes sortent d'abord.
6. Étant donné une vue qui lit le mémorisateur, quand elle le fait, alors elle reçoit une copie (`ChangedMsg.Failures`), jamais un pointeur sur l'état du routeur.
7. Étant donné les deux copies manuelles actuelles (`security.scanTarget.Failed`, `failedScans` d'OCI), quand cette story est livrée, alors elles sont encore en place ; leur retrait relève de A-08 et A-09a, ce qui garde cette story livrable seule.
8. Étant donné la clé, quand deux vues désignent la même cible, alors elles produisent la même clé : `Item.Target` (clé de cache de scan), chemins passés par `filepath.Clean` au lancement ; un dépôt a son chemin absolu en `ws` et dans `:sec`, une image sa référence brute (`repo:tag`) dans OCI et dans `:sec`. Un test de clé commune couvre les images sans tag (`<none>`) et les références écrites autrement (`nginx` contre `docker.io/library/nginx`). Une image et un dépôt ne sont pas la même cible.

Étant donné une ligne sélectionnée en erreur, quand l'échec arrive, alors un `Error` de 3 s le dit (`Failed to scan … — <cause>`) ; ensuite, tant que la ligne est sélectionnée, un `Status` persistant donne la cause lisible (`⊗ <cible>: last scan failed — <cause>`), jamais `err.Error()` brut non rédigé pour l'écran.

8. Le texte est identique pour la même opération dans toutes les vues (un seul constructeur de phrase, test).

**Hors périmètre** : le câblage dans chaque vue (fait dans sa story de migration) ; les messages d'actions instantanées.

content.content:
1	# DEVDESK-148 (A-10b) — Explorer clone list: activity column, per-row footer, safe causes
2	
3	Story: `docs/product/activity-indicator/stories.md` §A-10b. UX: `ux.md` §1.1, §1.2, §5 (legend).
4	Inventory: `inventory.md` row "Explorer liste de clone" and gap 4 (parallel clones, criterion 2
5	corrected). Pattern copied from DEVDESK-142/145/147 (`:jobs` targets level is the closest
6	twin: `components.ItemIndicator` + `DescribeItem`, D98). Security condition inherited from
7	**D97** (`docs/backlog.md`, DEVDESK-140 plan Q-A option C): the raw `err.Error()` written by
8	`explorer/clone_jobs.go:25,38` (and `app/forge_index.go:204`, see Q4) must be rewritten by
9	A-10b before the footer shows it, because a git/forge error can carry a URL with credentials.
10	
11	Out of scope: the forge index walk (except Q4), auth, the tree (A-10a, merged), the
12	clone pipeline itself (`pipeline.go`), `:jobs`.
13	
14	## Blocking questions (user)
15	
16	| # | Question | Options | Recommendation |
17	|---|---|---|---|
18	| Q1 | **Glyphs for "cloned" and the remaining state** (story hypothesis: done = `◉`). The five `ItemState`s are queued, running, done (`cloned`), skipped (`already there`, and also a queued clone skipped by `esc`, Detail `cancelled`), failed. `components.ItemIndicator` already maps them for `:jobs`' targets level (D98, shipped): `◴`, `●/○`, `◉`, `⊖`, `⊗`. Legend extension labels are new (not in `ux.md` §5, which D10 validated). | **A** reuse `ItemIndicator` as is: cloned `◉`, already there / cancelled `⊖`; legend extension `◉ cloned (clone list)` · `⊖ already on disk, or not started (cancelled) (clone list)` · **B** cloned `◉`, but "already there" back to the row at rest (no glyph; D8 logic "nominal = no dot") — loses a state the criterion asks to keep · **C** other glyph choice (UX ticket) | **A**: same projection as `:jobs` targets for the same run (the user sees one alphabet for one run in two views), no new code path, D7 respected (`◉` = finished only, `⊖` = skipped). |
19	| Q2 | **What the kept Status column shows.** Today: `IconPending queued`, `<frame> cloning`, `IconOK cloned` (green), `IconSkipped already there`, `IconError failed`. The frame must go (criterion 2); the other icons now duplicate the dot, and Rule 121's amendment (D9) says the activity column replaces them. A cancelled queued clone reads `already there` today (wrong word, pre-existing). | **A** words only, coloured like `:jobs`' State word (`indicator.Style(ItemIndicator(state))`, D98: no green), `cancelled` when `Item.Detail == "cancelled"`; `colCloneStatusMin` 16 → 13 · **B** keep icons and today's colours (green `cloned`), drop only the frame (`cloning` without prefix); width unchanged · **C** A without the `cancelled` word fix | **A**: one alphabet with `:jobs` (D98), no green for done (Rule 125), and the cancelled row stops claiming "already there". |
20	| Q3 | **Criterion 2 wording differs between sources.** The brief relayed for this story says "only one blinks, the N−1 others are fixed `◴`". `stories.md` §A-10b (corrected after `inventory.md` gap 4) says "the running clones blink (**several rows may blink at once**), the others queued `◴`": clones run in parallel (`forge.pull.parallel_jobs`, `clone.go:112`, `pipeline.go`). | **A** follow `stories.md`: every running item blinks, queued items `◴` · **B** force one blinking row (would need a "leader" rule the registry does not have, and would show a running clone as `◴`, i.e. lie) | **A**: it is the validated story text and the only one true to the pipeline. With `parallel_jobs: 1` A and B are identical. |
21	| Q4 | **`app/forge_index.go:204` (raw `msg.err.Error()` of the index walk)** is listed by D97 as an A-10b condition, but the brief puts the forge index out of scope. The index cause is shown today in `:jobs` (targets level Detail column and footer, A-06). | **A** fix it here with the same helper (one line + one router test) · **B** leave it, open a bug | **A**: same helper, one line, closes D97 entirely; it is the cause text only, not the index feature. |
22	
23	Hypotheses (prudent default, no question):
24	- H1 **The footer describes the selected row in every state** (A-05 / `:jobs` targets level): `components.DescribeItem(jobs.KindClone, item).Detail` as `Status.Detail`, `cloneStatusLine()` as `Status.Text`. `RowStatusLine` keeps the progress last to give way (A-05 rule): at 60 columns the cause may be cut, the progress stays.
25	- H2 **A skipped (already on disk) clone gets a Detail** `alreadyOnDisk = "already on disk"` in `CloneEventMsg.Transition()`, so the footer reads `⊖ Clone of alpha/api skipped — already on disk` instead of a bare "skipped", and `:jobs` says why too. The Detail column then shows it (it was empty).
26	- H3 **Cause redaction lives at the producer**, in one helper of `internal/jobs`, applied to every `Transition.Detail` built from an `error` in this story (clone `cloneEnded`, `cloneWalkFailed`, Q4 index) and to the matching `log.Printf` in `handleCloneEvent`. It removes URL userinfo (`REDACTED` → `https://host/…`) and the value of `token`, `private_token`, `access_token` query parameters; nothing else (no classification of git errors, D97 point 1 keeps "check logs" elsewhere). `git.Clone` already passes the token by environment, so a leak needs a URL with userinfo (config or an `insteadOf` rewrite) — rare, but on screen and in screenshots.
27	- H4 **The run-end event is unchanged**: `failureSummary` (`Failed to clone alpha/api and 2 others — check logs`, 3 s `Error`) stays; it is a batch summary, not one row, so `FailureEvent` does not fit. After its timer the selected row's detail is back.
28	- H5 **No per-frame rebuild**: `handleFrameMsg` calls `m.clone.table.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)`; rows are rebuilt on `ChangedMsg` only. `Model.jobFrame` and `cloneRow.frame` are deleted. A new clone list copies the tree table's current phase (`m.table.BlinkPhase()`) so its first frame matches.
29	- H6 **`ActivityTables()` always reports `explorer/clone-list`**: the real table when `m.clone != nil`, otherwise a table built by the same constructor (`newCloneTable()`) resized to `m.width × m.height`. The guard builds the view with no run (`builtView`), and a table that appears only mid-clone could not be checked at 60 columns. Same constructor → same columns; nothing renders it.
30	- H7 **Rule 130**: `cloningShortcuts()` does not depend on the selected row; unchanged. A test pins that the key set is identical for a queued, running, done, skipped and failed selected row.
31	- H8 **Discovery order kept** (`SortColumn: -1`); the indicator column has no `Less`, so `.` cycles Repository → Status as today (Status keeps its `Less` on `State`).
32	- H9 `m.spinner.Tick` batched in `handleCloneDestinationSelected` is left as is (the load spinner; `handleSpinnerTick` ignores it outside a load). Not a row animation; the guard does not flag `spinner.Model.Tick`.
33	
34	## Width arithmetic (Rule 116, `cellPadding = 2`, inside = width − 2)
35	
36	| Layout | Required (min + 2 each) | Detail (Optional, 20+2) shown from |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| today: Repository 30, Status 16 | 32 + 18 = 50 | inside ≥ 72 → width ≥ 74 |
39	| Q2-A: dot 2, Repository 30, Status 13 | 4 + 32 + 15 = 51 | inside ≥ 73 → **width ≥ 75** |
40	| Q2-B: dot 2, Repository 30, Status 16 | 4 + 32 + 18 = 54 | inside ≥ 76 → **width ≥ 78** |
41	
42	At 60 (inside 58) the required set fits in both cases: dot + Repository (flex) + Status,
43	Detail dropped, `RenderedWidth() == 58`. The tester pins the threshold with a sweep (step 2).
44	
45	## Steps (TDD — tests first, each step green and mergeable alone)
46	
47	Base command for every step:
48	`go test ./internal/ui/forge/explorer/ ./internal/jobs/ ./internal/ui/indicator/ ./internal/app/ && go vet ./...`
49	Step 4 adds `mise run lint`, `go test -count=2 ./internal/app/`, `mise run test-race` (cgo).
50	
51	### Step 1 — Safe causes (D97, security) · S (parallel with 2)
